heat.hint: Use an infrared thermometer if you have one. Compare to the same point on an identical machine or to the last recorded baseline.

options.label: Coupling or the shaft between machines

heat_bearing.q: Did the heat start within a day or two of a grease PM?
heat_bearing.hint: Overgreasing is the most common cause of a bearing that ran fine for years and suddenly runs hot.

heat_bearing2.q: Is there any new noise along with the heat?
heat_bearing2.hint: Rumble, squeal, or a rhythmic click. Use the screwdriver stethoscope if the area is loud.

r_heat_overgrease.title: Overgreasing is the first suspect.
r_heat_overgrease.text: A full cavity churns grease, generates heat, and can blow the seals. Do not add more grease. The lubrication troubleshoot tree walks the heat-after-relubrication branch: overgreasing versus pre-existing fault versus wrong product.
first: Remove the relief plug or vent and let the bearing purge while running
Trend the temperature over the next hour; overgreasing heat falls as excess purges
Check the quantity actually applied against G = 0.005 × D × B

also.why: The worked Five Whys is this exact failure

r_heat_bearing_noise.title: Heat with noise points at the bearing itself.
r_heat_bearing_noise.text: Take the rolling element path and enter through Heat. The tree separates running heat with noise (bearing damage, contamination, lubrication starvation) from post-PM heat.
first: Note the sound type: squeal is starvation, rumble is surface damage, click is brinelling
Check for grease purge at the seals and any metal glitter in it
Confirm the fixing ring is on the drive side only on pillow block pairs

also.why: Metal in grease or oil confirms wear
Misalignment overloads the coupling-end bearing first

r_heat_bearing_quiet.title: Quiet heat on a bearing is often a load problem, not a bearing problem.
r_heat_bearing_quiet.text: Misalignment, pipe strain, soft foot, and axial preload from a fixing ring on the wrong side all load a bearing in a direction it was not designed for. It runs hot before it runs loud. If the hot bearing is the one nearest the coupling, treat alignment as the lead suspect.
first: Which bearing is hot: coupling end suggests alignment, outboard end suggests axial preload or belt tension
Check soft foot and pipe strain before condemning the bearing
On pillow block pairs confirm the non-drive bearing can float axially

also.why: Indicator setup, sag, and the validity check

heat_pump.q: Is the pump flow reduced or at zero?
heat_pump.hint: A pump running against a closed or nearly closed discharge turns all its power into heat.

r_heat_pump_deadhead.title: Heat with low flow: the pump is running near shutoff or dead-headed.
r_heat_pump_deadhead.text: A centrifugal pump at shutoff heats the liquid in the casing rapidly and can flash it. A positive displacement pump against a closed discharge is an emergency: stop it. The diagnose tree branches at pump type first for this reason.
first: Confirm discharge valve position and any downstream blockage
Positive displacement: check relief valve is present, set correctly, and not lifting continuously
Centrifugal: check minimum flow bypass if fitted

also.why: Why PD against closed discharge is different
Seal faces fail fast at shutoff

r_heat_pump_seal.title: Normal flow, hot seal area: seal face or flush problem.
r_heat_pump_seal.text: Mechanical seal faces need a film of liquid to survive. A blocked flush line, a seal plan that is not doing its job, or a seal that was run dry at startup all show up as heat at the gland with normal pump performance.
first: Check flush or quench line flow and any orifice or filter in it
Look for a thermal damage signature on the faces if the seal has been pulled
Compression packing: heat with no leakage means the gland is too tight; 40 to 60 drops per minute is correct

also.why: Never run a mechanical seal dry

heat_coupling.title: A hot coupling is absorbing misalignment.
heat_coupling.text: Flexible elements flex once per revolution when shafts are misaligned. That cyclic flexing is friction, and friction is heat. Elastomer spiders and grid couplings show it first. Gear couplings run hot when lubrication is gone.
first: Infrared reading on the coupling versus the shaft on either side
Check for rubber dust or grid wear debris around the guard
Take a fresh alignment reading; compare to the last recorded values

also.why: Soft foot, then alignment, then recheck after torque

heat_gearbox.title: Gearbox heat: oil first, then one bearing versus the whole housing.
heat_gearbox.text: Overfill, low level, wrong viscosity, a blocked breather, or the box running above its thermal rating. The gearbox tree separates whole-housing heat from a single hot bearing, and worm boxes from helical, because normal for one is a fault for the other.
first: Oil level with the machine stopped and settled
Oil condition: colour, smell, water crackle test
Breather clear and not painted over

also.why: Gear oil EP additives and viscosity
Input shaft alignment loads the input bearing
Level, viscosity, and the sight glass lie

heat_motor.title: Hot motor: rule out the mechanical causes before calling it electrical.
heat_motor.text: The motors tree separates one hot bearing from a uniformly hot frame, then amps, cooling, and VFD speed. The mechanical checks a millwright owns: is the driven load heavier than it should be, is the motor misaligned, are the motor bearings failing, is the cooling fan or fins blocked. Any of those raise current and heat with nothing wrong inside the motor.
first: Uncouple and run the motor solo if safe: does the heat go away
Motor bearing sound and temperature at both ends
Fan cover and cooling fins clear of dust, product, and grease

heat_pneu.title: Hot solenoid or compressor.
heat_pneu.text: A solenoid too hot to hold is usually a partially stuck spool holding the plunger off its seat, or a coil on the wrong voltage. A hot compressor is usually a cooling, oil, or intake filter problem. Enter through Valve not shifting for solenoids, or the compressor branch for supply.
first: Solenoid: listen for humming with the screwdriver stethoscope
Compressor: aftercooler fan and fins, oil level, intake filter

also.why: Solenoid coil ratings and IP class

r_heat_brake.title: A hot brake is a dragging brake.
r_heat_brake.text: Gap closed up by wear, a cocked armature, a coil or rectifier not fully releasing it, or a manual release lever half engaged. It is heating the motor and eating the lining.
first: Infrared on the brake versus the motor
Three-point gap
Coil voltage and rectifier

noise.hint: If you cannot hear it clearly over the plant, press a screwdriver tip to the housing and the handle to the bone behind your ear.

options.label: Crackle, like gravel in the pump

noise_squeal.q: Does it clear after a few minutes of running?
noise_squeal.hint: Squeal that clears is usually marginal lubrication. Squeal that persists is something else.

r_noise_squeal_clears.title: Squeal that clears is lubrication starvation at startup.
r_noise_squeal_clears.text: The bearing is running on a marginal film until it warms and the lubricant flows. It will not stay marginal forever. The bearing diagnose tree covers squeal that clears versus persists.
first: Check the last grease date and quantity against the interval
Cold environment: is the grease grade too stiff for the startup temperature
Oil-lubricated: level, and whether the oil ring or collar is picking up

also.why: Interval factors: temperature, vertical shaft, contamination
Oil ring minimum speed, splash level

r_noise_squeal_persist.title: Persistent squeal: bearing, or something rubbing.
r_noise_squeal_persist.text: A bearing squealing continuously is starved or damaged. A lip seal, labyrinth, or wear ring rubbing sounds similar. The bearing tree separates them by whether the sound tracks bearing temperature.
first: Temperature at the bearing versus the seal area
Stop, lock out, rotate by hand: a rub is often felt as a drag point
Check for a dry-running lip seal after a shaft was replaced

also.why: Independent rotation check finds the rub

r_noise_belt.title: Belt squeal is slip.
r_noise_belt.text: Belt squeal under load is a tension or glazing problem. Check tension by deflection, look for glazed or cracked belts, and confirm sheave alignment with a straightedge. A squeal only on startup is a belt sized for running load and slipping on inertia.
first: Deflection tension check per belt manufacturer
Sheave alignment and groove wear (a worn groove lets the belt bottom out)
Match sets on multi-belt drives: never replace one belt of a set

r_noise_rumble.title: Rumble is surface damage or contamination in a bearing.
r_noise_rumble.text: The diagnose tree asks whether the bearing is new or old. A new bearing rumbling is contamination or installation damage. An old bearing rumbling is fatigue spalling. Either way it is on a timer.
first: Pull a grease or oil sample: metal glitter confirms it
Trend temperature and vibration daily until replacement
Check installation history: was it pressed on through the rolling elements

also.why: Correct fit-up so the replacement does not rumble too
If it is a pump, the noise branch separates bearing from cavitation

noise_click.q: Where is the click or knock coming from?

r_click_bearing.title: A rhythmic click from a bearing is brinelling or a damaged element.
r_click_bearing.text: One click per revolution or per element pass means a dent in a race or a flat on a roller. Brinelling comes from static overload, impact, or vibration while stationary. False brinelling comes from sitting idle on a vibrating base.
first: Was this machine shipped, dropped, or hammered on during installation
Does it sit idle next to something that vibrates
Frequency of the click versus shaft speed

also.why: Never press through the rolling elements
Bearing defect frequencies and the four stages

r_click_pump.title: Knocking in a pump: check valves, cavitation, or a loose impeller.
r_click_pump.text: Reciprocating pumps knock when a check valve is worn or slow. Centrifugal pumps knock from cavitation collapse or a loose impeller nut. The diagnose tree branches at pump type.
first: Reciprocating: check valve branch under No flow and Knocking
Centrifugal: suction conditions and impeller security

r_click_coupling.title: A coupling clicking or knocking is worn or loose.
r_click_coupling.text: Worn grid, worn gear teeth, a spider with chunks missing, or a loose hub on a keyway all produce a knock at shaft speed, usually worst on startup and shutdown as the load reverses through the backlash.
first: Lock out and check hub-to-shaft fit and keyway condition
Inspect the flexible element for wear debris
Take alignment readings; a worn coupling has usually been absorbing misalignment

r_click_gearbox.title: Gearbox knock: tooth damage or excessive backlash.
r_click_gearbox.text: A knock at output shaft speed is a damaged tooth on the output gear; at input speed it is the input pinion. Check backlash and inspect through the inspection cover with the box locked out.
first: Oil sample and magnetic plug for chips
Backlash measurement against the manual
Bearing play at each shaft

r_noise_cav.title: Gravel-in-the-pump is cavitation.
r_noise_cav.text: Vapour bubbles forming at the impeller eye and collapsing. The cause is on the suction side: not enough NPSH available. The system chain tab covers the suction side, the diagnose tree has the noise branch.
first: Suction strainer, suction valve position, suction line for air leaks
Liquid temperature up or suction level down since it last ran clean
Pump running far to the right of BEP after a system change

also.why: Cavitation destroys seal faces and impellers

r_noise_hiss.title: Hiss is compressed air escaping.
r_noise_hiss.text: Enter through Air leaking audibly. The tree covers fittings, valve exhaust ports, rod seals, and the search method when you cannot find it. In a loud plant use the screwdriver stethoscope or an ultrasonic detector.
first: Is it continuous or only while an actuator moves
Valve exhaust port hissing at rest means internal leakage

also.why: Leakage runs 20 to 30 percent on unmanaged systems

r_hum_solenoid.title: A humming solenoid has a stuck spool.
r_hum_solenoid.text: The plunger cannot fully seat because the spool is not moving. The coil will burn out if left. Enter through Valve not shifting, then Solenoid hums.
first: Contaminated or wet air is the usual root cause
Check the FRL filter bowl and the dryer dewpoint

r_hum_motor.title: Motor hum that changed is worth checking mechanically first.
r_hum_motor.text: Do the instant-off test: hum that vanishes the instant power is cut is magnetic. A motor that started humming louder may have soft foot (frame distortion changes the air gap), a failing bearing letting the rotor drop, or single phasing. Soft foot is the millwright check.
first: Soft foot check at all four feet
Bearing sound at both ends
Then hand it to the electrician with those results

vib.q: Did the vibration change recently, or has it been like this a long time?
vib.hint: Recent change means find what changed. Long-standing means trend it and understand the signature.

options.label: Stable for a long time, or unknown

vib_recent.q: What changed around the time it started?

options.label: Nothing I know of, it crept up

r_vib_maint.title: Vibration after maintenance: alignment, soft foot, or pipe strain.
r_vib_maint.text: The three things that get disturbed by maintenance and all show up as vibration. Soft foot is checked first, no exceptions. Pipe strain is found by taking readings before and after connecting the piping.
first: Soft foot at every foot, under 0.002 inch
Alignment readings versus the recorded values
Readings with piping disconnected versus connected: any shift over 0.001 to 0.002 inch is pipe strain

also.why: Bearing installed wrong vibrates from day one
Tolerances and the rim and face math
Pipe strain, voids, and anchors: the installation faults behind alignment that will not hold

r_vib_process.title: Vibration that follows the process is hydraulic.
r_vib_process.text: Cavitation, running far off best efficiency point, entrained air, or recirculation. Fix the operating point and the vibration goes with it. The diagnose tree has the vibration branch under centrifugal.
first: Where on the curve is it running now versus design
Suction conditions and NPSH margin
Discharge throttled far below design flow: recirculation

also.why: How flow and system resistance interact

r_vib_crept.title: Vibration that crept up is wear.
r_vib_crept.text: A bearing developing surface damage, a coupling element degrading, or looseness growing. The bearing tree takes the recent change path under vibration. Lubricant analysis will often confirm it before you tear anything down.
first: Oil or grease sample for wear metals
Coupling element inspection
Foundation bolts and baseplate grout

also.why: Ferrography tells you what kind of wear
Coupling wear as a vibration source
Baseline, alarms, and rate of change

r_vib_stable.title: Long-standing vibration needs a signature, not a guess.
r_vib_stable.text: Take a spectrum, find 1x, and let the frequency family name the fault: synchronous, sub-synchronous, non-synchronous, harmonics, sidebands, or broadband. The vibration tree walks it from the reading to the cause.
first: Get a baseline reading in three axes at each bearing and record it
Compare to identical machines
Do not act on a single reading; trend it

r_vib_sleeve.title: Sleeve bearing vibration: oil whirl, or a collapsing oil wedge.
r_vib_sleeve.text: The sleeve path in the bearing tree covers oil whirl (sub-synchronous, just under half speed), oil supply loss, and metal in the oil. An oil pressure drop on a pressure-fed sleeve bearing is a shutdown, not a watch item.
first: Oil pressure and temperature trend
Clearance check at next opportunity
Vibration frequency: below running speed is whirl

r_vib_fan.title: Fan vibration: clean the wheel before anything else.
r_vib_fan.text: Most fan vibration is buildup unbalance. Lock out, block the wheel against windmilling, open the housing, and look. Then the drive, then the bearings, then balance.
first: Product on the blades
Belt tension and sheave gauge
Shaft play at the bearings

options.label: Process fluid at a pump shaft
At a flange or gasket joint
Oil or grease at a bearing housing or gearbox

r_leak_air.title: Air leak: locate it, then fix the connection or the component.
r_leak_air.text: Enter through Air leaking audibly. Fittings, exhaust ports, rod seals, and the search method are all covered. Most air leaks are push-in fittings with the tube not bottomed out.
first: Continuous or only during actuation
Ultrasonic detector, soapy water, or screwdriver stethoscope

leak_shaft.hint: Packing is supposed to leak. A mechanical seal is not.

r_leak_packing.title: Packing leakage is normal within limits.
r_leak_packing.text: 40 to 60 drops per minute is correct and is what cools and lubricates the packing. Zero drops means the gland is too tight and the sleeve is being burned. A stream means worn packing or a scored sleeve.
first: Count the drops
Gland nut adjustment in small, even steps, both sides
Sleeve condition when the packing is next changed

r_leak_mechseal.title: A leaking mechanical seal has failed. The question is why.
r_leak_mechseal.text: The failure analysis tab reads the evidence: thermal damage, chemical attack, installation damage, face wear pattern, fretting. Replacing without reading the old seal means the new one fails the same way.
first: Keep the old seal and read the faces before ordering
Shaft runout under 0.002 inch TIR before the new one goes in
Did anyone run it dry, even briefly

also.why: Cartridge clips, setting dimension, never lubricate faces
Third seal in a year: the worked example
Misalignment makes the shaft describe an arc through the seal

r_leak_flange.title: Flange leak: the gasket, the faces, or the bolting.
r_leak_flange.text: Extrusion means under or over torque. Blowout means wrong gasket for the pressure or reused gasket. Weeping after thermal cycling means the joint moved. Surface finish matters for spiral wound.
first: Flange face condition and surface finish
Torque pattern and passes used last time
Gasket type against service and flange type

r_leak_lube.title: Grease purging is normal. Oil leaking is not.
r_leak_lube.text: The lubrication tree separates grease purge (relief path working as designed) from oil leakage at a lip seal, labyrinth, sight glass, or breather. Heavy grease purge right after a PM is overgreasing.
first: Grease: how much and how soon after the PM
Oil: level dropping, and where it exits
Breather blocked pushes oil out of the seals

r_leak_rod.title: Rod seal leak: inspect the rod before replacing the seal.
r_leak_rod.text: A scored rod destroys new seals immediately. Side load from a misaligned mount wears rod seals fast. Enter the leak branch, rod seal.
first: Rod surface under a fingernail: any score you can feel is too much
Mounting alignment and whether the load is applying a moment

r_leak_hyd.title: Hydraulic leak: pressure injection injury risk first.
r_leak_hyd.text: Do not feel for a hydraulic leak with your hand. Fluid at 200 bar through a pinhole will pass through skin and glove. Use cardboard to find the spray. Depressurise, lock out, and verify before touching the joint.
first: Cardboard, not hands, to locate
Depressurise and verify zero before touching
Any injection injury is an emergency room visit regardless of how it looks

also.why: Leak branch: fitting types, hoses, rod, shaft seal
Seal material against the hydraulic fluid

r_leak_valve.title: Valve leak: stem packing, or a seat that will not close.
r_leak_valve.text: Stem: tighten the gland evenly, then repack with the stem inspected. Seat: check the actuator takes it fully closed before blaming the seat, and ask whether this isolation valve has been throttling.
first: Gland load
Actuator stops and bench set
How the valve is actually used

options.label: Motor runs but the driven machine does not turn
Motor will not start or turn
Brake will not release, or clutch will not engage

r_nomove_pump.title: No flow: prime, suction, rotation, or the pump itself.
r_nomove_pump.text: The diagnose tree branches by pump type. Centrifugal no flow is usually lost prime, closed suction, wrong rotation, or a sheared key. PD no flow is a check valve or a relief valve dumping everything back.
first: Rotation direction versus the casing arrow
Suction valve and strainer
Is the shaft actually turning: independent rotation check

r_nomove_pneu.title: No movement: pressure, valve, line, actuator, in that order.
r_nomove_pneu.text: Enter through No movement. The tree brackets from the FRL gauge to the actuator port. Most no-movement faults are supply or valve, not the cylinder.
first: Gauge at the FRL
Does the valve click when commanded

r_nomove_coupling.title: Motor turns, machine does not: the coupling has let go.
r_nomove_coupling.text: A sheared spider, a stripped grid, a hub spun on the shaft, or a sheared key. Lock out and look inside the guard. Then ask why it let go: overload or misalignment.
first: Element condition and hub-to-shaft fit
Key and keyway
Alignment readings before reassembly

r_nomove_motor.title: Motor will not turn: is it mechanical or electrical?
r_nomove_motor.text: The millwright check: lock out, uncouple, and try to turn the motor shaft by hand. If it is seized, it is a bearing. If it turns freely and still will not start powered, it is electrical. If the driven machine is seized, the motor was never the problem.
first: Lock out, uncouple, turn each shaft by hand
Seized motor: bearing failure path
Seized driven machine: that machine's module

r_nomove_lube.title: Centralized system not delivering: the approach depends on the system type.
r_nomove_lube.text: Progressive: one blocked point stops everything downstream. Dual-line: each injector is independent, so no delivery anywhere is the pump or the reversing valve. The tree has a no-flow branch by system type.
first: Identify the system type first
Progressive: find the blocked divider by the indicator pin
Reservoir level and pump output

r_nomove_hyd.title: Hydraulic actuator not moving.
r_nomove_hyd.text: The hydraulics tree brackets it: pump outlet at deadhead, then DCV, then actuator port, then heat survey. Lock out, support loads, bleed accumulators, and verify zero before opening any connection.
first: Pump running and reservoir level
Relief valve set point and whether it is dumping
Directional valve shifting

also.why: Contamination is the root cause of most faults

r_nomove_brake.title: Brake or clutch not moving: gap, lining, actuator.
r_nomove_brake.text: Load supported and locked out. Air gap at three points, lining thickness, then the coil voltage and rectifier, the air pressure, or the thruster stroke.
first: Manual release lever position
Gap against nominal and maximum
Voltage at the coil when energised

r_nomove_valve.title: Valve will not stroke: actuator first, then the valve.
r_nomove_valve.text: Air pressure at the actuator, positioner output, stops, hand-auto clutch on an electric actuator. If the actuator is fine, the valve is stiff or seized: packing, thermal binding, deposits, or years without moving.
first: Actuator moves the stem when commanded
Packing gland load
When was it last exercised

options.label: Belt or chain drive losing speed under load
Conveyor belt slipping, mistracking, or spilling

r_low_pump.title: Low flow: the pump, the suction, or the system.
r_low_pump.text: Pumps create flow. The system creates pressure. Low discharge pressure with a centrifugal pump usually means the system has changed, or the pump has worn (wear rings, impeller). PD low flow is slip through worn clearances or a relief valve partially open.
first: Compare current head and flow to the curve
Wear ring clearance on centrifugal
Relief valve setting and seat condition on PD

also.why: Flow versus pressure, and why it matters here

r_low_pneu.title: Slow or weak: pressure under load, then flow controls, then tubing.
r_low_pneu.text: Enter through Slow or weak. Set the regulator under load, not at rest. Undersized tubing between valve and cylinder is the fault that gets misdiagnosed as a valve or pressure problem.
first: Gauge at the actuator port during the stroke
One direction or both

r_low_belt.title: Losing speed under load is slip.
r_low_belt.text: Belt tension, glazing, worn sheave grooves, or the wrong belt section. Chain: stretched chain riding up the sprocket teeth.
first: Tension by deflection
Sheave groove gauge
Chain stretch measurement over a known number of pitches

also.why: Over-tensioning to cure slip kills bearings

r_low_gearbox.title: Gearbox output loss.
r_low_gearbox.text: A gearbox does not lose ratio; if output speed is low the input is low or something is slipping upstream. If output torque is low, look at heat and oil condition: a hot gearbox is losing power to friction.
first: Input speed check
Oil condition and level

r_conveyor.title: Conveyor: slip, tracking, spillage, and belt damage have their own tree.
r_conveyor.text: Walk it running from outside the guards, mark the belt position, then lock out and block the take-up before touching anything. Causes (structure, pulleys, buildup, seized idlers, loading, splices) are fixed before any idler is adjusted.
first: Is the belt running off at the same place on the conveyor, or the same place on the belt
Are all the idlers turning
Where is the take-up sitting

also.why: The two rules and the adjustment order
If it is the drive belt, not the conveyor belt

r_low_fan.title: Fan output down: the system moved before the fan did.
r_low_fan.text: Filters, dampers, and ducts change the operating point. If the system is unchanged, then rotation, cone clearance, and the wheel.
first: Filter differential and damper positions
Rotation arrow
Wheel to inlet cone gap

also.why: Fan laws and the system curve

r_low_comp.title: Compressor cannot keep up: is it loading, and where is the air going.
r_low_comp.text: Read the controller. If it loads and output is normal, the plant is taking it all: leak survey first. If it will not load or output is low, the compressor tree.
first: Controller fault log and loaded hours
Inlet valve opening on load
Leak survey downstream

also.why: Leakage is 20 to 30 percent on unmanaged systems

options.label: Pump output slowly drifting over hours

r_err_pump.title: Surging is air, suction, or minimum flow.
r_err_pump.text: Air entering the suction line, a suction level dropping to vortex, or a centrifugal running below minimum continuous flow and recirculating. All three show as surging flow and pressure.
first: Suction line joints for air ingress (watch for foam in the sight glass)
Suction level and vortex breaker
Operating point versus minimum flow

r_err_pneu.title: Erratic pneumatic cycle: supply consistency, signal logic, or sensors.
r_err_pneu.text: Enter through Erratic or intermittent, or through Cylinder moves but machine cycle does not advance. Sensor faults get misdiagnosed as pneumatic faults constantly.
first: Gauge the pressure through a full cycle
Sensor LEDs at each end position

r_err_slip.title: Slow drift over hours: interval slip or thermal growth.
r_err_slip.text: The pumps module covers interval slip. Thermal growth on a hot service changes alignment as it warms: a pump aligned cold runs misaligned hot unless thermal growth was compensated.
first: Was the alignment done cold with a thermal growth offset
Coupling condition
Readings hot versus cold

also.why: Laser systems compensate for thermal growth

r_err_belt.title: Speed hunting on a belt or chain drive.
r_err_belt.text: Intermittent slip under varying load, a belt riding up and down a worn groove, or a variable-pitch sheave with a worn mechanism.
first: Tension and groove condition
Load cycle versus the hunting

options.label: Metal in the oil or on the magnetic plug
Scored shaft, fretting, or discoloured bearing
Guard off, interlock jumpered, or a light curtain taped
Rust or water at a pneumatic exhaust
Damaged o-ring or seal (flat spot, spiral cut, chip)

r_vis_guard.title: A defeated safeguard is a symptom. Find the task or the nuisance behind it.
r_vis_guard.text: Restore it now, and then find out why it was off: a PM task that needs the guard removed, a process that cannot be seen, nuisance trips, or a device that failed. Each has a design fix. Restoring the guard without the fix means it is off again tomorrow.
first: What task needed it defeated
Is it tripping on nuisance (dust, alignment, a forklift)
Did the device fail and production could not wait

also.why: Design the guard for the maintenance that will happen
A modification to protective elements may need a PSR
The guard found off: the worked example

r_vis_metal.title: Metal in the oil: find out which metal.
r_vis_metal.text: Iron is gears, races, and shafts. Copper and tin are bronze cages, bushings, and thrust washers. Silicon is dirt. Ferrography tells you the wear mechanism from particle shape. Elemental analysis tells you which component.
first: Sample from the same point every time
Compare to the last sample, not to a generic limit
Magnetic plug: fine fuzz is normal, chips are not

also.why: Sleeve bearing: metal in oil branch
Bearing failure patterns by wear type

r_vis_oil.title: Oil appearance tells you what got in.
r_vis_oil.text: Milky is water. Dark is oxidation. Foamy is air ingestion or the wrong oil. Varnish is oxidation deposits. The oil appearance branch covers each.
first: Crackle test for water
Smell for oxidation
Foam that persists versus clears

r_vis_purge.title: Heavy purge is overgreasing.
r_vis_purge.text: A little purge at the seals is the relief path working. A lot, especially right after a PM, is too much grease. Overgreasing causes more bearing failures than undergreasing.
first: Quantity applied versus G = 0.005 × D × B
Was the relief plug removed during greasing

r_vis_bearing.title: Read the failure pattern before ordering the replacement.
r_vis_bearing.text: Discolouration is heat. Fretting on the shaft or housing is a loose fit or the bearing walking. Scoring is contamination. A wear track off-centre on a race is misalignment. The pattern tells you the root cause; replacing without reading it repeats the failure.
first: Photograph the races, elements, and shaft before cleaning anything
Shaft and housing fits measured against spec
Fixing ring position on pillow block pairs

also.why: Bearing failure patterns: thermal, abrasive, corrosion, smearing
Measuring the seat and the bore before the new bearing

r_vis_gasket.title: Extrusion is torque. Blowout is the wrong gasket.
r_vis_gasket.text: Under-torqued gaskets extrude outward under pressure. Over-torqued gaskets crush and extrude inward. Blowout is a gasket not rated for the pressure, or one that was reused.
first: Torque values and pattern used
Gasket rating versus line pressure and temperature
Flange face flatness

r_vis_coupling.title: A coupling shedding rubber or grid metal has been absorbing misalignment.
r_vis_coupling.text: Coupling elements are sacrificial. When one wears out early, the misalignment that wore it is still there and is also loading the bearings and seals on both machines. Replace the element, then find the misalignment.
first: Alignment readings before the new element goes in
Soft foot
DBSE set correctly

r_vis_water.title: Water at the point of use means the dryer or drains are not working.
r_vis_water.text: Rust in cylinders, water from exhausts, ice at orifices in winter. The air quality tab covers dryer types, dewpoint, drains, and what to check.
first: Dryer dewpoint reading
Auto drains cycling
Bypass valve position

r_vis_oring.title: The damage shape tells you what happened.
r_vis_oring.text: Flat spot: pinched during assembly. Spiral cut: twisted going in. Chipped face: dropped. Swollen: chemical incompatibility. Hard and cracked: heat. Installation damage is the most common and the most avoidable.
first: Lubricate the o-ring, not the seal faces, on assembly
Chamfers and lead-ins on the bore
Material against the fluid

overload.q: With the machine locked out and uncoupled, does the driven machine turn freely by hand?
overload.hint: This one check splits the problem in half.

options.label: No, it is stiff or seized

overload2.q: Is the driven machine a pump?

r_ovl_seized.title: A seized or stiff driven machine is a bearing until proven otherwise.
r_ovl_seized.text: High amps and overload trips because the motor is dragging a failing bearing. Also possible: a rub, a seized seal, product packed in the casing. Turn each element independently to find which one drags.
first: Independent rotation check on each element
Feel for a drag point versus uniform stiffness

r_ovl_pump.title: A pump pulling high amps is doing more work than designed.
r_ovl_pump.text: Centrifugal: running far to the right of the curve (discharge wide open, low head), or pumping a denser or more viscous liquid than designed. PD: viscosity up, or discharge restricted with the relief valve holding it. The diagnose tree covers heat and vibration branches that overlap with this.
first: Discharge pressure versus design; wide open discharge overloads a centrifugal
Liquid density and temperature versus design
PD: relief valve set point and discharge restriction

also.why: Why PD amps rise with discharge restriction and centrifugal amps rise with flow

r_ovl_other.title: Free-turning machine, high amps: misalignment, or the motor itself.
r_ovl_other.text: Misalignment raises motor current measurably. Fix soft foot and alignment, then re-measure amps. If still high, it is the motor or the load profile, and the motors module (planned) covers the handoff to the electrician.
first: Soft foot, then alignment, then amps again
Belt tension if belt driven: over-tension loads the motor bearings

options.label: Sour, rotten egg, Monday morning smell
Fuel or solvent where there should not be any

r_smell_burn.title: Burning smell: oxidised oil, a slipping belt, or a bearing about to let go.
r_smell_burn.text: Oxidised oil has a sharp varnish smell and turns dark. Belt slip smells like burning rubber. A bearing running to failure smells like hot metal and grease. Find which one with an infrared thermometer.
first: Infrared survey of every bearing and the coupling
Oil colour and smell at the sight glass
Belt guard: rubber dust and heat

r_smell_sour.title: Sour smell is microbial growth in the oil or coolant.
r_smell_sour.text: Bacteria living at the water and oil interface. Worst after a weekend shutdown when the system sits still. Tramp oil and water are the food. The contamination tab covers biocide intervals and tramp oil removal.
first: Water content test
Tramp oil skimming
Biocide per the fluid supplier

r_smell_solvent.title: A solvent smell where none should be: check what the seals are made of.
r_smell_solvent.text: A seal or hose that is incompatible with the fluid swells, softens, and lets it through. The compatibility table covers 19 fluids against five materials.
first: Seal and hose material against the actual fluid
Look for swelling at any exposed elastomer

r_smell_elec.title: Hot electrical: motor windings or a solenoid coil.
r_smell_elec.text: A motor that smells of burnt insulation has failed windings: isolate it and find the mechanical cause before the rewind. A solenoid coil cooking from a stuck spool smells the same at the valve. Find it by nose and by infrared, then lock out.
first: Which component is hot
Motor: the burnt-winding branch, then the handoff package
Solenoid: pneumatics, stuck spool branch

symptoms.sub: Squeal, rumble, knock, crackle, hiss, hum

symptoms.name: Leak
symptoms.sub: Air, oil, grease, process fluid, water

symptoms.name: No output or no movement
symptoms.sub: Motor runs but nothing happens, or nothing runs at all

symptoms.name: Low or falling output
symptoms.sub: Flow, pressure, force, or speed below spec

symptoms.name: Erratic or intermittent
symptoms.sub: Surging, hunting, random stops, works sometimes

symptoms.name: Something looks wrong
symptoms.sub: Metal in oil, discoloured oil, scoring, cracked parts, rust

symptoms.name: Motor overloading or tripping
symptoms.sub: High amps, overload trips, breaker trips on start

symptoms.name: Smell
symptoms.sub: Burning, hot oil, sour, solvent, ozone
